policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's proper name 'Harsith' distinguishes the qere reading; the alternative-rendering note concerns English wording and does not alter that textual judgment.
ASV's 'I will bring' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv spellings, and no mapped textual-variant note decides between them; retain the base qere fallback.
